patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Todoist share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Linear only if your buying job matches “Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo ” rather than Todoist's shape. Choose Todoist only if your buying job matches “Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/” rather than Linear's shape. Workflow advantage: Linear leans work-management; Todoist leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Todoist share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Linear is Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo annual.; Todoist is Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$6.25/user/mo annual; Business ~$10..
- Company-size focus: Linear (startup, small-business, mid-market) vs Todoist (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Linear-leaning work-management vs Todoist-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Linear — Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Todoist — Not a Work OS or portfolio tool.

Limitations — Linear: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Leaner automation than Jira Enterprise; Todoist: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool; Team features mainly on Business.

Poor-fit cases: Linear is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS · Todoist is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool · Avoid Linear if you actually need Todoist's motion (Personal and team task manager with natural-language capture — Free; Pro from ~$)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
